newsitem.title: USA: British tourist survives skydiving accident.
newsitem.headline: British tourist survives skydiving accident.

text.p: A novice British skydiver was in serious condition on Tuesday after surviving a 12,000-foot (3,650-metre) fall by landing on his veteran instructor, who died in the accident.

Gareth Griffith, a 21-year-old management consultant from London, fractured his spine in the jump on Sunday when his parachute did not open properly, a spokeswoman at Orlando Regional Medical Centre said.
He also suffered injuries to his abdominal organs and several broken ribs. The injuries were not life threatening and he was not paralysed, she said.

Michael Costello, 42, of Mount Dora, Florida, was killed in the fall. An instructor for 18 years, he was jumping in tandem with Griffith, a common practice for veterans jumping with novices, his business partner, Wilma Godwin, said.
The main parachute deployed but failed to open after the pair jumped from a Cessna Caravan airplane, police reports said. A backup parachute was deployed but also failed.
Costello hit the ground with Griffith on top of him, police said. The two were jumping at a rural airport in Umatilla, Florida, about 30 miles (48 km) northwest of Orlando.
Griffith and five friends were enrolled in a two-week skydiving course, Godwin said.
